description:
Workspace-architectural decision: every extension-server crate has at least one ~350-475 line handle_*_set handler that exceeds clippy::pedantic's too_many_lines threshold (100) by ~3x. The canonical mail-server has a 2578-line email.rs whose handle_email_set is the largest. Splitting in any sibling without first splitting the canonical violates workspace AGENTS.md 'Canonical Templates'.

## Current sizes (selected from JMAP-x2gd.58 survey)

- jmap-chat-server: handle_message_set 474L, handle_chat_set 373L, handle_space_set 363L, handle_emoji_set 355L
- jmap-mail-server: email.rs 2578L (handle_email_set), mailbox.rs 1195L, submission.rs 984L, sieve.rs 1218L, mdn.rs 607L

Other extension-server siblings likely have analogous sizes (audit pending).

## Two paths

**(a) Accept the size, silence the lint.** Mark each long /set handler with #[allow(clippy::too_many_lines)] on the canonical mail-server and propagate the allow attribute to every extension-server sibling in the same pass. Document in workspace AGENTS.md 'Canonical Templates' that the one-big-fn-per-/set-handler shape is deliberate.

Pros: zero code churn. Preserves cookie-cutter consistency. Lint stops being workspace-wide noise that hides the next legitimate hit.

Cons: 350+ line handlers stay difficult to review and to test in isolation. The 'cookie-cutter consistency' argument is partly self-fulfilling — if mail-server is canonical, the size is canonical, and the size argument never loses.

**(b) Split each /set into per-op sub-functions.** Refactor jmap-mail-server first (canonical), then propagate the same split to all extension-server siblings in the same pass. Each /set's create/update/destroy paths become named sub-fns; the orchestrator shrinks to ~50 lines.

Pros: per-sub-fn testability. Easier review (each sub-fn is ~50-100 lines). Lint passes naturally.

Cons: ~140-200 sub-functions across the workspace (8 extension-server crates × ~16-25 sub-fns each). Large coordinated commit. Cross-cutting test infrastructure changes if any per-op sub-fn needs distinct fixtures. Risk of bugs introduced by the mechanical refactor.

## Recommendation

The bead JMAP-x2gd.58 (chat-server review) recommended this workspace-arch decision be made before any chat-server-local action. Both paths are plausible; the choice is workspace-architectural.

If (a) is chosen: the implementation is ~1 line per handler × ~25 handlers across 8 crates plus the AGENTS.md policy note. Small.

If (b) is chosen: file per-crate epic children. Land mail-server first per canonical-template rule. Propagate to siblings. Budget for review churn.

## Engineering basis

- bd:JMAP-x2gd.58 (chat-server review) directly.
- Workspace AGENTS.md 'Canonical Templates' propagation rule.
- clippy::pedantic too_many_lines lint threshold = 100 lines (default).
- Mail-server canonical email.rs:2578 directly.

## Related

- bd:JMAP-ljr6 (workspace const fn sweep) — same canonical-template propagation pattern but for a different lint.
- bd:JMAP-8zcl (workspace canonical-template sweep for 'Authorisation contract' rustdoc) — same shape but for docs.
title: Workspace-arch decision: handle_*_set handler sizes (~350-2578 lines) vs clippy::too_many_lines
